issue_context.title: PWSH 7.2.1: invoke-webrequest hangs at: VERBOSE: received -byte response of content type text/plain
issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] Write a descriptive title.
- [X] Make sure you are able to repro it on the [latest released version](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases)
- [X] Search the existing issues.
- [X] Refer to the [FAQ](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/docs/FAQ.md).
- [X] Refer to [Differences between Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell](https://docs.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/whats-new/differences-from-windows-powershell).

### Steps to reproduce

While attempting to download a file from the following URL, invoke-webrequest hangs seemingly indefinitely with no indication of why. The 'Reading Response' displays, so it seems to actually download the data, but just hangs after doing so. The PWSH window is not responsive to Ctrl+C.

*NOTE*: If testing the below, replace the useragent string with a valid 'Company Name' and 'email address' as per below U.S. sec.gov Webmaster FAQs. When I ran the command I use my own email address with my own custom string (changing the user agent string to something completely different didn't change anything):
https://www.sec.gov/os/webmaster-faq#developers

However, the following equivalent Windows PowerShell 5.1 command works perfectly so seems regression:
$test=invoke-webrequest -uri 'https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000008177/000156761917000512/0001567619-17-000512.txt' -useragent 'Private Investor EMAIL@ADDRESS.COM' -usebasicparsing -method get -verbose
PS C:\WINDOWS\system32>

WORKAROUND on Windows only:
$test=& 'powershell.exe' "(invoke-webrequest -uri 'https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000008177/000156761917000512/0001567619-17-000512.txt' -useragent 'Private Investor EMAIL@ADDRESS.COM' -usebasicparsing -method get).content"

### Expected behavior

```console
PS C:\Windows\System32>$test=invoke-webrequest -uri 'https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000008177/000156761917000512/0001567619-17-000512.txt' -useragent 'Private Investor YOUREMAILADDRESS@EMAILDOMAIN.COM' -SkipHeaderValidation -method GET -verbose
PS C:\Windows\System32>
```


### Actual behavior

```console
PS C:\Windows\System32>$test=invoke-webrequest -uri 'https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000008177/000156761917000512/0001567619-17-000512.txt' -useragent 'Private Investor YOUREMAILADDRESS@EMAILDOMAIN.COM' -SkipHeaderValidation -method GET -verbose
VERBOSE: GET with 0-byte payload
VERBOSE: received -byte response of content type text/plain
```


### Error details

_No response_

### Environment data

```powershell
$PSVersionTable

Name                           Value
----                           -----
PSVersion                      7.2.1
PSEdition                      Core
GitCommitId                    7.2.1

PSCompatibleVersions           {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0…}
PSRemotingProtocolVersion      2.3
SerializationVersion           1.1.0.1
WSManStackVersion              3.0
```

comments: @TravisEz13 @PaulHigin Maybe for WG-Security. Infinite cycle in Regex https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/a5d41c22871c4835de2a0f8ba17d553fa777c6a3/src/Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility/commands/utility/WebCmdlet/StreamHelper.cs#L435

@WG-Security
WG-Security group looked at this and there is potential for infinite recursion on the regex (s_metaexp) string (line 414) and DOS attack.
There should be fuzz testing along with a fix, and this can be done by using text files for fuzzing source.

Note that dotNet has added code to remove some potential infinite recursions, when possible.  But we shouldn't count on it.
@iSazonov This issue is fixed in `PowerShell 7.4.0 preview 1`

review_comments:
You could easily have an embedded style sheet large this.   

The issue says the response header said it was text.  We should not be running this code on text.

Since we can not implement full HTML parser we can only address common scenarios. From my understanding first tag always `<html>`, then `<head>` and then common recommendation is to have `<meta>` tag on top place as best practice. The code follows this.
Also best practice is to have encoding tag in HTTP header so here we address an edge case in which the best practice is ignored.
If we put a limit like this in, we should have an error or warning when it exceeded and possibly expose the limit value as a parameter so people can make it work.
